notes.made: One of the first songs cut for the album, in Studio A at Warner's Amigo Studios, with Lee Herschberg engineering onto a 3M 79 24-track through a custom API desk. Lenny Waronker and Russ Titelman hired Steve Gadd on drums (behind a baffle under an umbrella mid-room), Willie Weeks on bass, Buzzy Feiten on acoustic guitar doubling Neil Larsen's electric piano, and Ernie Watts, Tom Scott and Chuck Findley on horns, whose parts Jones sang to them. Victor Feldman's Rhodes part was replaced by Larsen's and Feldman moved to vibes; Jones played the guitar on the bridge and did the finger snaps herself.
notes.context: Jones, Tom Waits and their friend Chuck E. Weiss were living at the Tropicana Motel in Los Angeles when Weiss vanished and then phoned Waits from Denver to say he'd fallen for a cousin there. Waits passed the news on and Jones wrote it up, adding a last-line twist that never happened. She played it on Saturday Night Live in April 1979, it reached 4 on the Hot 100, and in February 1980 she won Best New Artist over the Knack and Dire Straits, with the song up for Song of the Year.

listen_for.note: Gadd's shuffle, played with straight sixteenths against the swing. Herschberg told Mix he often sounded like two drummers.
Jones's own guitar comes in here, and the finger snaps are hers too.
Watts, Scott and Findley playing parts Jones hummed to them, recorded with two mics set well back so they blend into one sound.

leads_to.title: Extremely Cool
leads_to.why: The man himself, twenty years later, on an album Tom Waits co-produced and played guitar all through.

notes.unverified: Wikipedia gives the single release as 28 April 1979, after the SNL spot; Mix says it peaked in May. I left the single date out. The album credits also list Jeff Porcaro and Michael McDonald, but not on this track, so no thread to them.

culture.title: Saturday Night Live
culture.line: Jones promoted the album on Saturday Night Live in April 1979, playing Chuck E.'s in Love and Coolsville.

culture.title: Number 4
culture.line: It reached 4 on the Hot 100 and 18 in the UK in 1979, and the album went to 3.

culture.title: Best New Artist
culture.line: On 27 February 1980 Jones won Best New Artist over the Knack, Dire Straits, the Blues Brothers and Robin Williams, and the song was up for Song of the Year.
